A1.justification: Both PDFs present PaceLLM with readable text, figures, tables, equations, and complete Appendices A–E. Pages 3–26 match exactly in extracted text and rendered appearance; the limited differences on pages 1–2 are fully inspectable.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, activation visualizations, and inference-time measurements in Section 4 and Appendices A, B, and E.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, visualizations, inference-time measurements, and additional-model results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices C–D retain the same activation memory bank, retrieval and update procedures, cortical-expert clustering, and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same LongBench, ∞-Bench, NIAH, and MMLU tasks and test scenarios. The detailed appendix evaluations introduce no coverage differences between versions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the reported comparisons, including LongLLMLingua, SnapKV, and Activation Beacon in Table 2 and the vanilla-model comparisons in Tables 7–9.

E3.justification: The training-free and low-cost fine-tuning settings, model configurations, NIAH testing procedure, ablation configurations, and SDPA/FlashAttention timing comparisons are identical.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same CE/PA component comparisons, layer/threshold/noise ablations in Table 5, activation analysis in Figure 4, and inference-efficiency analysis in Appendix A.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged. Tables retain point estimates, and checklist item 7 repeats the same determinism-based justification without adding run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–9 and graphical results in Figures 3–4 are identical, including the inference timings and additional-model results in the appendices. No numerical values or reported findings change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20 and the mathematical formulations of clustering and memory updates are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about brain-inspired FFN mechanisms, model-agnostic applicability, benchmark improvements, and context extension to 200K tokens.

C2.justification: The working-memory analogy, CE/PA synergy interpretations, task-specific ablation explanations, and acknowledged computation/storage overhead remain unchanged, including the appendix discussions.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, 4×A100-40G hardware disclosure, appendix algorithms and timing information, and checklist statements about releasing code and data upon acceptance are identical.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 51 references are unchanged. The introductory RAG clause containing citations [49, 33, 38] moves from page 2 to page 1 without changing research positioning or cited works.

P1.justification: v3 removes Kangcong Li and Peng Ye's equal-contribution designation, relabels the same corresponding authors with asterisks instead of daggers, and updates the version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Small spacing changes on page 1 bring the introductory RAG sentence continuation over from page 2, leaving additional whitespace there. Figures, tables, and all page layouts from page 3 onward are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 changes author annotations and slightly reflows the opening pages while retaining all methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including Appendices A–E. These administrative and small layout edits leave the paper's overall scientific and explanatory quality materially unchanged.
